chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abi Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

He said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, is not unjust to His servants, but rather He, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Among them is one who is unjust to himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds by Allah's permission.' He said: The one who is unjust to himself is the one who believes in part [of the truth] and disbelieves in part. The moderate one is the one who believes in all [of it]. The one who is foremost in good deeds is the one who believes in all [of it] and acts upon it.

key_terms.ظَالِمٌ لِنَفْسِهِ: Unjust to himself (one with partial faith)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the three types of believers mentioned in the Quran according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s (peace be upon him) exegesis of the three spiritual tiers from Surah Fatir, distinguishing between the 'unjust to himself' (who possess faith but are negligent), the 'moderate' (who maintain consistent faith), and the 'foremost in good' (who excel in both belief and righteous deeds). This classification underscores the Shia emphasis on the dynamic nature of Iman, where faith is not static but measured by the degree of active adherence to divine commandments.
